name: HTML5 Web Storage ("Super Cookies")
location: Firefox: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\<randomtext>.default\webappstore.sqlite ; Chrome: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\Local Storage ; Edge: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\<Profile>\Local Storage
purpose: Per-domain, text-based persistent storage (up to 10MB per domain) that websites use for state and tracking data — functionally a "super cookie" that outlives typical cookie settings.
normal_baseline: Storage entries correspond to sites the user actively uses (web apps, SaaS logins, e-commerce carts) with reasonable per-domain data volume.
anomalies: Local Storage data present for a domain never visited according to browsing History, suggesting cross-site tracking, a compromised ad/tracking script, or staged payload data
A per-domain storage blob approaching the 10MB cap, well beyond typical application state
Storage entries encoding obfuscated, base64, or otherwise encoded script content rather than typical application state
parsing_tools: ccl_chrome_indexeddb (CCL / obsidianforensics — LevelDB Local Storage parser)
anti_forensic_notes: Web Storage is cleared only when a user clears "site data" (not just cookies/history) or removes the profile, so it survives many routine cleanup actions and is less commonly targeted precisely because it is less well known than cookies.
interpretation: Chrome and Edge store Local Storage as LevelDB databases — a binary key-value store requiring a LevelDB-aware parser rather than a text editor, since keys can remain in unflushed .log files. Firefox uses SQLite (webappstore.sqlite). Legacy IE/EdgeHTML stored the equivalent data in XML files.
